disagreements.issue: Whether an initially empty writable audit mount can implement a no-reread boundary and what payload descriptors may remain.

Prefer a bounded one-way pipe, with a narrower no-host-input claim only as a fallback if the mount remains.

Remove every writable host mount; use null stdin and separately bounded O_WRONLY stdout/stderr pipes to a trusted drain that never replies or varies behavior from content/status while cognition is live.

resolution.rationale: A writable directory is readable and observable by its writer, so the fallback is rejected. Receipt bytes known to the payload are not themselves forbidden; forbidden feedback is auditor interpretation, counters, scores, prior receipts, comparisons, acknowledgments, conditional closure/throttling, EPIPE, or host response. The drain continuously consumes both streams using frozen content-invariant behavior, stores at most each separate cap plus count/digest evidence, silently discards excess while cognition lives, and reports overflow only after termination as NOT_RUN.
resolution.selected_position: No writable /out or host mount; /dev/null stdin; exact O_WRONLY stdout and stderr pipe FDs only; all other payload FDs closed and verified through proc fd/fdinfo; a bounded non-signaling external drain never writes back.
resolution.required_change: Replace the proposed output mount and impossible reread assertion with the frozen pipe topology, separate byte maxima and emitted-byte counts, invariant drain protocol, overflow/drain-failure NOT_RUN semantics, and production-profile FD canaries.
